02 // Strategic Context

Executive Summary & Objectives

Tracking historical reliance on hydrocarbon fuels versus renewable and nuclear power is essential for policy evaluation and ESG investment analysis.

Core Analytical Objectives

The project was designed to deliver a single, unified analytical interface enabling cross-filtering across multi-dimensional metrics (geography, fuel mix, volume, and clean energy share).

  • Per-Capita Footprints: Evaluate national and regional energy consumption across 200+ sovereign economies.
  • Decarbonization Trajectories: Monitor 60-year historical shifts from hydrocarbon baseloads to renewables.
  • Multi-Dimensional Cross-Filtering: Seamless interaction between geospatial maps, ranking leaderboards, and temporal area charts.

03 // Data Warehousing

Phase 1: BigQuery SQL Integration

Synthesizing independent data streams in Google Cloud BigQuery while resolving grain inconsistencies and composite key alignment.

BIGQUERY SQL composite_fact_table_join.sql 
-- Multi-part composite primary-foreign key join across Entity, ISO Code, and Year
SELECT
  t1.Entity,
  t1.Year,
  t1.Solar,
  t1.Wind,
  t1.Coal,
  t1.Oil,
  t1.Gas,
  t1.Biofuels,
  t1.Hydropower,
  t1.Nuclear,
  t1.`Traditional biomass`,
  t2.`Total energy supply`
FROM `energy-data-508810.Energy.sources` AS t1
LEFT JOIN `energy-data-508810.Energy.use per person` AS t2
  ON t1.Entity = t2.Entity 
 AND t1.Code = t2.Code 
 AND t1.Year = t2.Year;
ETL Hurdle A

Mixed Granularity Resolution

The raw Entity field included sovereign states ("Germany", "India") alongside continental and economic aggregates ("World", "OECD (EI)", "Europe", "High-income countries"). Leaving these combined caused severe double-counting.

Engineering Fix

Implemented advanced filtering logic across visuals to exclude non-sovereign macro entities, guaranteeing clean peer-to-peer benchmarking.

ETL Hurdle B

Geocoding Classification

Standard text fields failed to map reliably across historical territories without explicit geocoding metadata.

Engineering Fix

Explicitly reclassified the Entity column's Data Category to Country/Region, enabling Power BI's Bing/Azure mapping engine to resolve sovereign boundaries dynamically without latitude/longitude coordinates.

04 // Semantic Layer

DAX Mathematical Modeling

Calculation logic engineered with defensive programming principles, variable caching (VAR), and divide-by-zero mitigation (DIVIDE).

DAX MEASURE Total_National_Energy_TWh 
Total_National_Energy_TWh = 
SUM(Energy_Data[Coal]) + 
SUM(Energy_Data[Oil]) + 
SUM(Energy_Data[Gas]) + 
SUM(Energy_Data[Biofuels]) + 
SUM(Energy_Data[Solar]) + 
SUM(Energy_Data[Wind]) + 
SUM(Energy_Data[Hydropower]) + 
SUM(Energy_Data[Nuclear]) + 
SUM(Energy_Data[other renewables]) +
SUM(Energy_Data[Traditional biomass])
DAX MEASURE Clean Energy % 
Clean Energy % = 
VAR CleanTotal = 
    SUM(Energy_Data[Solar]) + 
    SUM(Energy_Data[Wind]) + 
    SUM(Energy_Data[Hydropower]) + 
    SUM(Energy_Data[Nuclear]) + 
    SUM(Energy_Data[Biofuels]) + 
    SUM(Energy_Data[other renewables])
VAR TotalEnergy = [Total_National_Energy_TWh]
RETURN
    DIVIDE(CleanTotal, TotalEnergy, 0)
DAX MEASURE Fossil Fuel % 
Fossil Fuel % = 
VAR FossilTotal = 
    SUM(Energy_Data[Coal]) + 
    SUM(Energy_Data[Oil]) + 
    SUM(Energy_Data[Gas])
VAR TotalEnergy = [Total_National_Energy_TWh]
RETURN
    DIVIDE(FossilTotal, TotalEnergy, 0)
05 // Analytical Findings

Strategic Insights Uncovered

Key energy transition patterns and structural market realities synthesized from the multi-decade dataset.

01

The Modern Transition Inflection (Post-2010)

While coal and oil dominated baseload growth through the late 20th century, solar and wind exhibit exponential adoption curves beginning around 2010, particularly in Europe and East Asia.

02

Macro Concentration of Supply

The top 5 energy-consuming nations account for over 50% of aggregate global primary energy use, demonstrating that global net-zero goals hinge disproportionately on policy execution in a few key markets.

03

The Baseload Reality

Despite rapid renewable additions, hydrocarbon consumption (oil and natural gas) remains historically resilient, indicating that clean energy is currently augmenting new demand rather than fully replacing legacy fossil infrastructure in most developing economies.
